transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Tom Avery (LH Head of Eng), Sara Blake (LH IT Security), Raj Patel (LH Platform PM), Nina Gomez (LH DevOps)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining today, uhm this is the official onboarding kickoff for Lighthouse Health and Redwood, i'll do a quick intro then pass to diego and priya to walk technical and operational stuff.
[00:12] Tom Avery: thanks maya, excited to get started, we have a few constraints to cover up front.
[00:17] Maya Chen: great, can you give us a quick run through of the current stack and what you're trying to accomplish for the pilot?
[00:27] Tom Avery: sure, so we're building an in-product assistant for clinicians, needs to connect to internal EHR metadata, low latency is important  target p95 under 200ms for short queries  and all data residency and audit logs are required.
[00:40] Sara Blake: and from security side we need SOC2 evidence, SSO via SAML, customer-managed KMS for keys, we also want audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[00:52] Diego Ruiz: yes, we can support SAML/SSO and KMS/HSM integrations, and we have audit logs export. for network we typically support VPC peering or private endpoints for Private deployments. for Dedicated we can do a reserved pool in a customer VPC as well.
[01:08] Nina Gomez: can you clarify dedicated in VPC? we prefer not to route traffic over the public internet.
[01:12] Diego Ruiz: absolutely  Dedicated can be provisioned in a customer VPC or via VPC peering depending on cloud. we will share the subnets, route table, and security group requirements; often we do an AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink.
[01:23] Raj Patel: any specifics on ports and CIDR ranges? our security team will need that for approval.
[01:28] Diego Ruiz: yes, i'll send a network checklist. typically for inference endpoints you'll need outbound to our control-plane IPs for enrollment, and then traffic can be kept internal for inference depending on the setup. we'll include NAT / IGW notes if needed.
[01:44] Priya Nair: high level timeline  we usually do a 4-6 week pilot. week 1 is network + SSO, week 2 is model selection and sample traffic, week 3-4 is pilot runs and perf tuning, final week for rollout/playbooks. is that okay?
[01:58] Tom Avery: sounds good, we were hoping for a 6-week pilot to validate latency and cost metrics.
[02:03] Maya Chen: perfect, pilot scope  diego, can you outline the default pilot config you recommend?
[02:09] Diego Ruiz: for their workload based on what you said (short queries, low latency), i'd recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs, single-model endpoint pinned to an open LLM we vet, KV cache enabled for prefix reuse, and batching tuned conservatively to preserve p95 latency. we'll instrument with Console probes and tracers so we can see token-level latency and cost.
[02:32] Sara Blake: we also prefer to have encryption keys in our KMS, not Redwood-managed. can you support CMK/HSM?
[02:38] Diego Ruiz: yes, we integrate with customer KMS providers  we'll share the KMS integration guide. for HSM we have an enterprise path.
[02:45] Tom Avery: what's the rollback / fallback plan if load spikes or we see higher-than-expected latency?
[02:50] Maya Chen: Redwood has routing fallback policies  we can route to a lower-cost hosted variant or autoscale the Dedicated pool depending on your policy. we configure canary rollouts and automatic fallback if latency or error thresholds are breached.
[03:06] Raj Patel: about logging and PII  we need to ensure PHI is never retained outside our control. is there a private deployment option?
[03:14] Diego Ruiz: yes, Redwood Private (on-prem or VPC-controlled) ensures customer data never leaves your environment besides control-plane signals; we also support data-retention policies and configurable KV cache TTLs, and you can disable logging of raw prompts in the platform.
[03:27] Sara Blake: good to know, can we get a SOC2 artifact and do you have a data-processing agreement?
[03:32] Priya Nair: yes i'll send SOC2 report and the DPA, plus SSO/SAML and KMS docs after the call.
[03:40] Tom Avery: rough success criteria  p95 latency < 200ms, availability 99.9 for the pilot, and cost per 1k tokens under our target  we'll define exact numbers in the success doc.
[03:51] Maya Chen: noted  priya will own the success criteria doc and circulate.
[03:56] Nina Gomez: network schedule  i can do a deep-dive next week, prefer 5/12 morning PST.
[04:03] Diego Ruiz: works for me. i'll block time.
[04:06] Maya Chen: ok next, integration touchpoints  access to a staging EHR instance, sample query set, and test service account for SSO will help us validate hooks.
[04:18] Tom Avery: we'll provide a staging API and a test service account, but need to scrub PHI in samples.
[04:24] Maya Chen: understood, anonymized samples are fine.
[04:27] Raj Patel: can we run a short benchmark with our traffic shape? what's needed from our side to run that?
[04:33] Diego Ruiz: we need representative request traces, typical sequence length distribution, and concurrency targets. with that we can recommend batching windows, quantization, and kernel configs; we'll run a perf sweep during week 3 of pilot.
[04:47] Sara Blake: also want to confirm RBAC and least-privileged access for consoles and logs.
[04:52] Priya Nair: Redwood Console supports RBAC and scoped API keys, plus audit trails. we'll include role templates for your security review.
[04:59] Tom Avery: ok, on timelines who will send what and when?
[05:03] Maya Chen: i'll summarize. priya will send SOC2 and contract/DPA, diego will send network checklist and schedule the deep-dive, i'll send onboarding checklist and provisioning steps for Dedicated trial. tom/raj will share traffic and staging creds.
[05:17] Raj Patel: noted. can you also share a sample architecture diagram for Dedicated in a VPC?
[05:21] Diego Ruiz: yes, we'll include the diagram and the subnet/security group examples.
[05:25] Nina Gomez: any restrictions on outbound to specific IP ranges? firewall will need that.
[05:29] Diego Ruiz: we'll provide the control-plane IP ranges and endpoints; for Private deployments we can avoid public egress for runtime.
[05:36] Tom Avery: what about support SLAs during pilot and production?
[05:40] Maya Chen: pilot gets standard support; for Dedicated customers we offer enhanced SLAs as part of the reserved contract. we can discuss upgrade paths depending on commitment.
[05:49] Sara Blake: do you have legal or procurement items we should be aware of? any standard exceptions?
[05:53] Priya Nair: we have a standard enterprise agreement; i'll loop in legal if there are non-standard terms.
[05:59] Maya Chen: quick note on costs  we'll provide an estimate for the pilot based on 2 GPUs and your expected token volumes; Redwood Optimize will also suggest batching and quantization options to lower per-token cost.
[06:12] Tom Avery: perfect. any gotchas for on-prem?
[06:15] Diego Ruiz: on-prem has extra ops work  packaging, network isolation, and hardware compatibility checks. we provide an installer and checklist, but it typically adds lead time. for now based on your constraints Dedicated in VPC is the fastest path.
[06:30] [PAUSE, crosstalk]
[06:33] Nina Gomez: one more network question  will we need peering across accounts if we use separate prod and staging accounts?
[06:38] Diego Ruiz: yes you can peer per account or set up Transit Gateway depending on scale. we'll advise in the network deep-dive.
[06:46] Maya Chen: okay, to wrap up let's recap action items and next steps. priya?
[06:51] Priya Nair: i'll send SOC2, DPA, SSO/KMS docs by tomorrow (2027-05-09); diego will send network checklist and propose 5/12 for deep-dive; maya will provision Dedicated trial and share access steps; tom/raj will share anonymized traffic and staging creds by 5/14; i'll circulate pilot success criteria doc by 5/11.
[07:12] Tom Avery: thanks everyone. excited to get the network thread moving.
[07:15] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.
